tabs.title: Platform Apps setup
tabs.summary: Enter Credovation’s Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps once — every company then connects with a sign-in button.
tabs.html:
How it works

The Super Admin sets up one sign-in app per platform, once, in Settings → Platform Apps. After that, every company connects its own accounts by clicking Connect in Integration. It signs in on the platform’s own page and never sees App IDs or secrets.

Until a platform is saved, companies see that channel as “Not enabled yet”, with no Connect button.

Already using these apps for SMC? You can use the same Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps. Enter the same IDs and secrets here. In each app, also add this platform’s callback URL (below), and the lead permissions listed for that platform.

On each card:

  1. Paste the ID and Secret → Save.
  2. Register the callback URL(s) shown on the card in the platform’s developer console, exactly as shown (https, no trailing slash).
  3. Click Test and fix anything marked in red.
Platform Callback URL Webhook URL
Meta (Facebook & Instagram) {{metaCallback}} {{metaWebhook}}
LinkedIn {{linkedinCallback}} {{linkedinWebhook}}
Google {{googleCallback}} —

Meta — Facebook Lead Ads and Instagram Lead Ads

  1. developers.facebook.com → My Apps → open the Credovation app, or Create app (type Business).
  2. Add the use cases for Lead Ads (capture and manage ad leads) and Facebook Login for Business. Menu names can change slightly when Meta updates its dashboard.
  3. Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs → add {{metaCallback}}.
  4. App settings → Basic:
    • App Domains: add {{baseDomain}}
    • Privacy Policy URL: {{privacyUrl}}
    • Terms of Service URL: {{termsUrl}}
    • User data deletion → Data deletion instructions URL: {{dataDeletionUrl}}
    • Copy the App ID and App Secret into the Meta card → Save.
  5. Click Test. It checks the ID and secret, checks App Domains, and subscribes the lead webhook for you (Page → leadgen → {{metaWebhook}}). If it can’t, do it by hand: Webhooks → Page → Subscribe, with the Callback URL {{metaWebhook}} and the Verify token from the card, then subscribe to leadgen.
  6. Switch the app to Live.
  7. Permissions the connectors ask for: leads_retrieval, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_metadata, pages_manage_ads, ads_management and business_management. Instagram also asks for instagram_basic.
  8. For companies other than Credovation:
    • Until Meta approves Advanced Access for the permissions above, only people with a role on the app (Administrators, Developers, Testers) can connect.
    • To get Advanced Access: App Review → Permissions and Features → request Advanced Access for each permission (screen recording plus use-case text), and complete Business Verification of Credovation.
    • Until it’s approved, add client users as Testers (App roles → Roles).

Use-case text for App Review: “CredoOne is a lead management system. A business connects its Facebook Page so that the people who fill its Lead Ad forms are added to its CRM as leads. We list the user’s Pages so they can choose which to connect, subscribe the Page to leadgen webhooks and read each lead’s form answers.”

Screen recording (1–3 min):

  1. Sign in to the company console → Integration → Facebook Lead Ads → Connect.
  2. Consent notice → Facebook login → permission screen → pick the Page → Connected.
  3. Create a test lead with the Lead Ads Testing Tool → the lead appears in Leads.

LinkedIn — Lead Gen Forms

  1. linkedin.com/developers/apps → open the Credovation app, or Create app linked to the Credovation Company Page. A Page admin must Verify it (Settings tab).
  2. Auth tab:
    • Authorized redirect URLs → add {{linkedinCallback}}.
    • Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the LinkedIn card → Save → Test.
  3. Products tab → request Lead Sync API. LinkedIn reviews this. If it can’t be added next to the app’s other products, create a second app just for it and use that one here.
  4. The scopes used are r_marketing_leadgen_automation, r_ads and r_organization_admin.
  5. Webhooks tab (when available for the app) → add {{linkedinWebhook}}. LinkedIn validates it automatically, and responses then arrive within seconds. Without it, responses are fetched every 15 minutes.

LinkedIn logins last about 60 days. After that, companies see “Reconnect”.

Google — Google Sheets / Google Forms

  1. console.cloud.google.com → the Credovation project.
  2. APIs & Services → Library → enable Google Sheets API.
  3. OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform):
    • Data access → add the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly.
    • Home page {{platformUrl}}, privacy {{privacyUrl}}, terms {{termsUrl}}, and the authorised domain for {{baseDomain}}.
    • Audience → Publish app.
  4. Credentials → OAuth client ID (Web application) → Authorised redirect URIs → add {{googleCallback}}. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the Google card → Save → Test.
  5. Until Google verifies the app, users see “Google hasn’t verified this app” and click Advanced → Go to CredoOne. This works for up to 100 users. Submit for verification to remove the warning.

Privacy contact

The Privacy contact card sets the email, grievance officer, legal name and address. They appear on every consent notice and on the public pages the platform apps link to:

  • {{privacyUrl}}
  • {{termsUrl}}
  • {{dataDeletionUrl}}

It starts as support@credovation.tech. Change it if privacy requests should go elsewhere. Currently: {{privacyEmail}}.

2. **Auth** tab:

tabs.title: Connecting channels
tabs.summary: What a company does to connect Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn or Google Sheets — and what to tell them.
tabs.html:
For company users (2 minutes)

  1. Integration → the channel card → Connect with Facebook / LinkedIn / Google.
  2. Read the consent notice (DPDP Act). Click I agree to all & connect, or tick each purpose and click Continue. Nothing is pre-ticked: consent must be a clear action. Who agreed, when, from which IP and which notice version are all recorded.
  3. A secure window opens on facebook.com / linkedin.com / accounts.google.com. Sign in with your own ID and password. CredoOne never sees them.
  4. On the platform’s screen, keep every permission box ticked, and select your Pages (Facebook) or Business.
  5. Back in CredoOne, pick what to connect:
    • Facebook: Pages
    • Instagram: Instagram professional accounts
    • LinkedIn: ad accounts and Pages
    • Google: paste the sheet link and pick the tab
  6. Click Connect. Recent leads are fetched straight away, then:
    • Facebook / Instagram: new leads arrive in seconds (Page lead webhook), with a check every 15 minutes as a safety net.
    • LinkedIn: instant when LinkedIn notifications are on, otherwise every 15 minutes.
    • Google Sheets: new rows every 15 minutes. Each row is read once.

Facebook and Instagram are separate connectors

They sign in the same way (Instagram lead ads are delivered through Facebook), but each has its own card, its own Pages and accounts, and its own stats.

When both are connected for the same Page:

  • Facebook-placement leads go to Facebook Lead Ads.
  • Instagram-placement leads go to Instagram Lead Ads.

When only one of them is connected, it receives both placements, so no lead is lost.

Disconnect = withdraw consent

Disconnect on the connector:

  • unsubscribes the Pages
  • deletes the stored login immediately
  • stops new leads

Leads already received stay. Reconnect at any time.

Status you may see

Status Meaning What to do
Not enabled yet The Super Admin hasn’t saved that platform in Platform Apps Super Admin → Platform Apps
Connected Leads are flowing —
Reconnect needed / Login expired The platform login expired or was revoked (LinkedIn: about 60 days) Open the connector → Reconnect
Disconnected Consent was withdrawn Reconnect, or delete the connector
“Real-time off … fetched every 15 minutes” on a Page The Page couldn’t be subscribed to the lead webhook Check you have the Advertise task on the Page; allow CredoOne in Meta Business Suite → Settings → Integrations → Leads access

tabs.title: REST API & webhooks
tabs.summary: Website / landing-page forms, WhatsApp Business Platform and generic REST — all authenticated with the connector’s API key.
tabs.html:
One model for every push channel

Website / Landing Page Form, WhatsApp Business Platform and REST API / Webhook all work the same way: the sender POSTs to the connector’s endpoint and proves it is allowed with the connector’s API key.

Any one of these authenticates the request:

  • header x-api-key: <API key>
  • ?key=<API key> in the URL, for senders that can’t set headers (Meta Cloud API, plain HTML forms)
  • x-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the API key>

Calls without a valid key get 401. Fields like name, phone, mobile, email, message, city and utm_* are mapped automatically. Use Field mapping for anything else.

curl -X POST '{{platformUrl}}/api/intake/<connector key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-api-key: <API key>' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: form-1042' \
  -d '{"name":"Riya Sen","phone":"9876543210","email":"riya@example.com","message":"Full body checkup","consent":"yes"}'

Responses:

  • 200 — created or merged (includes leadId)
  • 202 — accepted but failed; it is retried automatically every 15 minutes
  • 401 — wrong or missing key
  • 429 — slow down

Send the same Idempotency-Key header on retries, and the lead is never duplicated.

Website / Landing Page Form

  • From your server or form plugin (Elementor, Contact Form 7, Webflow, Wix): add a webhook to the endpoint with the x-api-key header, or put ?key= in the URL.
  • Plain HTML form: action="<endpoint>?key=<API key>". After submitting, people land on the hosted thank-you page.
  • Browser fetch: works too, but the key is visible in the page source. Rotate it if it is misused.

Keep a hidden _hp field: submissions where it is filled in are treated as bots.

WhatsApp Business Platform

  • Meta Cloud API: set the Callback URL to <endpoint>?key=<API key> and the Verify token to the API key, then subscribe to messages.
  • BSPs (Interakt, AiSensy, Gupshup, WATI…): point the incoming-message webhook at the endpoint and add the x-api-key header.

Older connectors

Website-form and WhatsApp connectors created before this change still accept deliveries without the key, so live sites don’t break. Their Setup tab shows Require API key: update the form or Callback URL first, then click it.

tabs.title: Company modules & access
tabs.summary: Pause or restrict any module or sub-module for one company, on top of its plan.
tabs.html:
Where

Company → Edit (or Create) → Modules tab.

Every module and sub-module comes from the module registry, so new ones appear here automatically after each deploy.

Three settings per row

Setting Effect
Plan default (modules) / Follows module (sub-modules) Uses the plan’s access. Change the plan and this follows.
Custom Tick exactly which of Create, Read, Update and Delete this company gets. You can restrict below the plan, or give more than the plan. A sub-module can never go beyond its module.
Paused Switches the module (or sub-module) off for this company. The module stays in its menu marked Paused and shows a notice; its data is kept. Set it back to Plan default to resume.

What it affects

  • Every user of the company, the owner included. Changes apply within about 30 seconds, with no sign-out needed.
  • Role Management inside the company: the grid is capped by these settings, so paused or restricted actions can’t be granted. Roles saved earlier are capped automatically.
  • The API: paused or restricted actions are refused on the server, not only hidden in the screens.

Reset all to plan removes every override for the company.

tabs.title: Troubleshooting
tabs.summary: The exact messages platforms show, why, and the fix.
tabs.html:
First check, always: Super Admin → Platform Apps → Test on the platform. It confirms the ID and secret, checks App Domains and the lead webhook (Meta), and lists the exact URLs to register.

What you see Cause Fix
Card says “Not enabled yet” That platform isn’t saved in Platform Apps Platform Apps → enter the ID and secret → Save → Test
Popup: “This sign-in link has expired” More than an hour passed, or the link was reused Click Connect again
Nothing opens after “I agree” The browser blocked the popup Use Open the sign-in window, or allow popups for the site
Facebook: “URL blocked” / redirect URI is not whitelisted Callback missing in the Meta app Add {{metaCallback}} under Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs
Facebook: “Feature unavailable … updating additional details for this app” The person has no role on the Meta app, and Advanced Access isn’t approved yet Add them as a Tester, or get Advanced Access + Business Verification
Facebook: “App not active” App in Development mode Switch the app to Live
Facebook: “Invalid Scopes: leads_retrieval …” The Lead Ads use case isn’t added to the app Add the use case and permissions (Platform Apps setup)
“Connected without a permission we need” A box was unticked on Facebook’s screen Connect again and keep every box ticked
“No Facebook Pages came back” Pages weren’t selected, or the person isn’t a Page admin Reconnect and select the Pages, or ask a Page admin
Instagram account greyed out Not a professional account, or not linked to a Page Switch to Professional and link it to the Facebook Page
Page shows “Real-time off” The Page couldn’t install the app (task or Leads access) Advertise task on the Page; Meta Business Suite → Integrations → Leads access → allow CredoOne. Leads still arrive every 15 minutes.
Leads arrive only every 15 minutes (Meta) The app’s Page leadgen webhook isn’t set Platform Apps → Meta → Test (it sets it), or add it in Webhooks
LinkedIn: “redirect_uri does not match” Callback missing on the Auth tab Add {{linkedinCallback}}
LinkedIn: “unauthorized_scope_error” Lead Sync API not approved for the app Request Lead Sync API in Products
LinkedIn: “No ad accounts or Pages came back” The person lacks an ad-account role Account Manager, Campaign Manager or Leads Manager on the ad account
Google: “Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch” Callback not on the OAuth client Add {{googleCallback}} under Authorised redirect URIs
Google: “access_denied — app is being tested” Consent screen in Testing Publish the app, or add the user as a test user
Google: “This Google account can’t open that sheet” Sheet not shared with that account Share the sheet, or sign in with its owner
Connector says “Login expired — reconnect” The token expired or was revoked Open the connector → Reconnect
Website form / WhatsApp returns 401 The API key is missing from the call Send x-api-key, or add ?key= to the URL (REST API & webhooks)

Deleting a client

What you see Cause Fix
No delete icon on a client row The role doesn’t have Delete on Client → Clients, or Super Admin has restricted or paused it for the company Role Management → tick Delete on the Clients sub-module
“Could not send OTP … Create an active webhook for the ‘Delete OTP’ event” No active webhook for delete_otp Settings → Webhooks → add one for Delete OTP (verification)
“Add your WhatsApp number to your profile to receive delete OTPs” Neither your profile nor the company has a WhatsApp number Add your number in your profile
“OTP expired. Request a new one.” More than 5 minutes passed Close the dialog and start again
“Too many wrong attempts.” 5 wrong codes Request a new code
A client was deleted by mistake — Nothing is lost: the whole client, with its sales orders, invoices, pay-ins and tickets, is archived in your company’s database (and the delete is in the activity log). Ask your administrator to restore it.

tabs.html:
What this is

Every company gets its own Android (and, once signing is set up, iOS) app, built from one shared source. The build runs on GitHub Actions in this platform's own repository, the finished signed file is uploaded to that company's own S3 folder, and the company downloads it from its Mobile App page.

Nothing is built on this server, and no signing key is ever stored on the platform. The keys live in the build repository's GitHub secrets, where a build can use them and nobody can read them back.

Super Admin → Company → Mobile App → Build
        ↓
GitHub Actions  (build-mobile.yml)   ← signing keys live here
        ↓
S3   <COMPANY CODE>/app/<platform>/<version>/<file>
        ↓
Company → Mobile App → Download

1. The repository

The app source is the mobile/ folder of this repository, and the workflow is .github/workflows/build-mobile.yml. Both are already in the code you deploy — push them to the branch you build from, and open the repository's Actions tab once so Actions are enabled for it.

If you would rather keep the app in a repository of its own, copy mobile/, .github/workflows/build-mobile.yml and .github/scripts/report.mjs into it and point GITHUB_BUILD_REPO there instead. Nothing else changes.

2. Platform settings

Set these where the platform runs (Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables), then redeploy:

Variable What to put
GITHUB_BUILD_REPO owner/repo of the repository above
GITHUB_BUILD_TOKEN A fine-grained token with Actions: read and write on that repository
GITHUB_BUILD_REF The branch to build from — leave empty for the default branch
GITHUB_BUILD_WORKFLOW Leave empty unless you renamed build-mobile.yml
MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET A long random value. The same value goes in the repository's secrets — it is how a finished build proves it is yours
MOBILE_BASE_VERSION 1.0.0 — builds are numbered 1.0.0.1, 1.0.0.2, … per company
MOBILE_PACKAGE_PREFIX e.g. in.credoone.lms → each company gets in.credoone.lms.<code>
MOBILE_IOS_SIGNING 1 only after step 4

The Mobile App tab shows each of these as green or red under Your set-up now, so you can check without leaving the screen.

3. Repository secrets — Android

GitHub → the repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:

Secret What to put
MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET The same value as on the platform
S3_BUCKET / AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_REGION The bucket the platform uses, with write access
ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 base64 of your .jks keystore
ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS
ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD

Do this before the first Android build. Android only installs an update when it is signed with the same key as the installed app. Without these secrets the build stops rather than signing with a throw-away key — because a throw-away key means staff must uninstall the app, and lose anything held on the device, to take the next version.

Make the keystore once, for every company, on any machine with Java (keytool comes with it):

keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore release.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 \
        -validity 10000 -alias credoone
base64 -w0 release.jks > release.jks.b64      # macOS: base64 -i release.jks -o release.jks.b64

Paste the contents of release.jks.b64 into ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, and keep release.jks somewhere safe — losing it means no company's app can ever be updated again.

With the GitHub command line, from the repository folder:

gh secret set MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 < release.jks.b64
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD

4. Repository secrets — iOS (optional)

iOS needs an Apple Developer account. Add IOS_CERT_P12_BASE64, IOS_CERT_PASSWORD, IOS_PROFILE_BASE64 and IOS_TEAM_ID as secrets, then set MOBILE_IOS_SIGNING=1 on the platform. Until then, the iOS button stays switched off and says why.

5. The first build

  1. Super Admin → a company → Mobile App.
  2. Check the app name, the application id and the colour, upload a 1024×1024 icon, and Save.
  3. Build Android. It takes 10–20 minutes; the row shows Queued → Building → Ready and links to the run on GitHub.
  4. When it says Ready, download the .apk on an Android phone, allow "Install unknown apps" for the browser, and sign in with a staff login of that company.
  5. Build again and install over it — it must update without uninstalling. If Android says "App not installed", the signing key changed: check step 3.

The apps are native screens, not the website in a frame. They talk to the address the company uses — its own domain where it has one, otherwise its platform address — over HTTPS, so that address must be reachable from phones. Changing a company's address needs a new build.

6. What the app shows

The Mobile Modules tab decides which modules the apps may show, and each user's role decides what they may open. Both are read when the app starts, so changing either needs no new build. A new build is needed only for the name, icon, colours, application id or address.

At the first sign-in the app shows the company's DPDP notice, which must be scrolled to the end before it can be accepted — and every acceptance appears under DPDP → Acceptance status, marked as coming from the app.

7. If something goes wrong

Message What it means
GitHub refused the build (404) The workflow file is not on the branch, or Actions have never been enabled. Push .github/workflows/build-mobile.yml and open the Actions tab once.
GitHub refused the build (401 / 403) GITHUB_BUILD_TOKEN is wrong, expired, or lacks Actions: read and write on that repository.
Not set up yet — missing … One of the platform settings in step 2 is empty. The red lines under Your set-up now name them.
ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 is not set The build stopped on purpose. Finish step 3 first.
App not installed on the phone The build was signed with a different key than the installed app. Use the same keystore.
Build stuck on Building The run failed without reporting back. Open the run on GitHub; the nightly housekeeping job marks builds older than 90 minutes as failed.
Nothing arrives in S3 The repository's AWS secrets cannot write to the bucket, or S3_BUCKET differs from the platform's.

The signing key (from v1.7.0)

Android refuses an update signed with a different key than the installed app — it says "package conflicts with an existing package". So an app needs one key for its whole life.

Set MOBILE_SIGNING_SECRET on the platform and it takes care of this for you: at a company's first Android build it makes one permanent key for that company and signs every later build with it. You never handle a keystore.

How it is kept safe:

  • the keystore and both passwords are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before they are stored, under MOBILE_SIGNING_SECRET. The database on its own cannot sign anything.
  • the key is never a workflow input — inputs are printed in the run's own log. The build collects it over the same signed channel it reports its result on, only while it is still running, and deletes the file when it finishes.
  • nothing in the key ever reaches a browser. Super Admin → Company → Mobile App → Android signing shows the alias, the version it applies from and the certificate fingerprint, and nothing else.

If you keep your own keys instead, leave MOBILE_SIGNING_SECRET empty and add the four ANDROID_* secrets to the repository as before — the build uses the platform's key when there is one, yours when there is not, and fails with a clear message only when there is neither.

One reinstall, once. A phone holding an app built before the platform's key needs a single uninstall-and-reinstall. Every update after that installs over it. The Build screen says so, per company, and only while it is still true.

Connect it in either of two ways; the panel shows both, with the values filled in:

  2. A repository webhook — Payload URL <your platform>/api/public/webhooks/github/push, content type JSON, the same secret, "Just the push event".

Either way the body is signed, so nothing else can start a build. A push to any other branch is accepted and ignored. A company with no app yet is skipped — a first build fixes the application id and the signing key, so it is always started by hand.

tabs.title: Chats, notices and push
tabs.summary: How one-to-one and group chat works, how a notice reaches every screen, and the one setting that makes it all instant.
tabs.html:
What this is

Chats is messaging inside one company — one-to-one and groups — on the web and in the company's own app. Alongside it, Notices puts a line of scrolling text across the top of every screen, and push notifications reach a phone that is not open.

A member is known to other members by name and role only. A phone number or an e-mail address is never part of anything chat sends, so a group cannot be used to collect contact details. That is in the code, not a setting.

Switching it on

Chats is a module, so it starts switched off — like every new module.

  1. Super Admin → Plans: tick Chats on each plan that should have it. A module absent from a plan grid has no permissions at all.
  2. Super Admin → Company → Modules: confirm it is not paused for that company.
  3. Company → Settings → Role Management: give the roles that should administer chat the two sub-modules:
    • Groups — create and change groups.
    • Notices — post and stop the scrolling notice. Everyone else needs only Chats › read and create, which is what lets them message and be messaged.
  4. Mobile Modules (Super Admin → Company → Mobile Modules): tick Chats for it to appear in the app.
  5. Rebuild the company's app from Mobile App → Build if the installed app was built before v1.6.0. The app reads permissions and modules at start-up, so those need no rebuild — only the new screen does.

Making it instant

Chat works with nothing configured: every screen asks the platform every few seconds, and the header says "Messages refresh every few seconds."

To make it instant, give the platform one real-time service. This server cannot hold a WebSocket open — it runs on Vercel — so a managed service holds the connection and the platform publishes to it.

Pusher (the default, and the one with a Mumbai cluster):

  1. Create a free Sandbox app at pusher.com → Channels. Choose cluster ap2 (Mumbai) — the nearest to India, which is what keeps a message to a few tens of milliseconds.
  2. Copy its four values into the environment:
REALTIME_PROVIDER=pusher
PUSHER_APP_ID=…
PUSHER_KEY=…
PUSHER_SECRET=…
PUSHER_CLUSTER=ap2
  1. Redeploy. The header now says "Messages arrive the moment they are sent."

Ably instead, if you prefer it: REALTIME_PROVIDER=ably and ABLY_API_KEY=…. Nothing else in the platform changes — the whole difference is in one file (server/lib/realtime.ts).

The secret never reaches a browser or a phone. A client asks the platform to sign each channel it wants to listen on, and the platform signs only that person's own channels and the conversations they are actually in.

Push notifications

Push needs no key on the platform. Each company's app is built with Expo, and Expo's push service holds the Google (FCM) and Apple (APNs) credentials created with the app.

  • A phone registers itself when someone signs in, and is forgotten at sign-out — so a shared phone stops receiving the previous person's messages.
  • A token the device no longer holds is deleted the first time Expo says so. Other failures are counted, and a phone that fails five times is left alone.
  • A push is a courtesy, never the delivery: the message is already saved before the push is attempted. A phone that is off simply shows it later.

Notices

Chats → Notices → New notice. Up to 300 characters, in one of three tones (info, warning, success), optionally also sent as a push, with an optional stop time. It appears straight away on every screen, web and app.

  • A person can hide a notice on their own device; the next notice still shows.
  • On the phone, tapping the bar stops the scrolling so a long notice can be read.
  • Stop takes it down everywhere at once. The row stays in the list, so there is a record of what was said and when.

What is kept, and for how long

Super Admin → Company → Retention Policy has two rows for chat:

Row Default Notes
Chat messages Keep for ever A conversation is a record, not a log. Choose a period only if you have a reason to.
Dormant phones 180 days Measured from when the app was last opened, not when the phone was registered, so an active phone is never unregistered.

Creating or changing a group, and posting or stopping a notice, are written to Activity Logs like every other action.

If something looks wrong

  • No Chats menu. The module is not ticked on that company's plan, or the role has no Chats › read.
  • Messages only arrive after a few seconds. No real-time service is configured, or its keys are wrong. The chats header says which of the two is happening.
  • No notifications on the phone. Notification permission was declined on that phone (iOS asks once), the app is older than v1.6.0, or the phone has not been opened since the app was reinstalled. Signing out and in registers it again.
  • Someone cannot be messaged. They are inactive, or they belong to a different company. Chat never crosses companies: every channel name carries the company, and the platform refuses to sign a channel from another one.

Two kinds of build

They are different files, and neither does the other's job.

Direct install Store upload
Android .apk — anyone can install it from the company's download page .aab — Google Play only. It does not install on a phone; Google makes the phone-ready files from it
iOS ad-hoc .ipa — installs only on devices registered to the provisioning profile App Store .ipa — App Store Connect only. It does not install by hand

Pick with Store build on the company's Mobile App tab, or What it is for on Mobile App Release. The screen tells you which file you are about to get before you press the button.

A store build never appears on a company's download page, because handing somebody an .aab gives them a file that cannot work and no way to know why.

One-time set-up: Google Play

  1. Create the app in the Play Console with exactly the application id the Build screen shows (e.g. in.credoone.lms.whd). An id can never be changed once an app is published, so copy it rather than typing it.

  2. Upload one build by hand to any track. Google will not accept an unknown application id over the API, so the very first one has to go through the console. Download the .aab from the Build screen and upload it there.

  3. Make a service account — Play Console → Setup → API access → Create new service account → follow it into Google Cloud, make a key in JSON format, download it.

  4. Invite it back in Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite the service-account address → give it Release to testing tracks on your apps.

  5. Add the key to GitHub → the build repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:

    Name Value
    GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON the whole contents of the JSON file

One-time set-up: the App Store

  2. Make an API key — App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → generate a key with the App Manager role. You can download the .p8 once.

    Name Value

What you see What it is

"Invite the service account in Play Console → Users and permissions" The key is valid but has no permission on this app.

tabs.html:
November 2026 — v1.8.0 — publishing to Google Play and the App Store

  • Store build is a new choice when building an app. A normal build still gives you the file you install directly; a store build gives you the file Google Play and the App Store accept, which is a different thing entirely.
  • It can upload itself. Once your administrator has added the store credentials, a store build goes straight to Google Play's Internal testing track and to TestFlight. Without them the file is simply kept for you to upload by hand — both ways work.
  • Nothing reaches the public on its own: promoting a release, or submitting it for review, is always a decision somebody makes in the Play Console or App Store Connect.
  • Store builds are kept off your download page, because those files do not install on a phone.
  • New guide: Publishing to Google Play and the App Store.

November 2026 — v1.7.0 — one place for every app

  • Mobile App Release is a new Super Admin screen: every company's app in one place, with what is building now, what finished, what failed, and how many phones are on the newest version.
  • Build for one company, or for all of them at once. A company that has no app yet is left out of the bulk build on purpose — its first one is always started by hand.
  • A push rebuilds everybody. Switch on Automatic rebuilds, and new app code rebuilds the app of every company that wants it, each with its own name, icon and colours. Phones get it as an ordinary update.
  • Updates now install over the old app. The platform keeps one permanent signing key per company, so Android stops refusing updates. A phone holding an older app needs one uninstall-and-reinstall; the screen tells you when that applies, and only while it does.
  • The Mobile App tab on a company used to spin for ever if anything went wrong. It now says what went wrong, and has a Try again button.
  • The Build screen shows what is actually live — one card per platform with the version, size, file and a download — before the list of every build.

November 2026 — v1.6.0 — chat, notices and notifications

  • Chats is new, on the web and in your app: message anyone in your company one-to-one, or talk in a group your administrator sets up. A message appears for everyone the moment it is sent.
  • Members are shown by name and role only — nobody's phone number or e-mail address is visible in chat, ever.
  • A group has a name and the people added to it. You can see who is in it, and leave one you no longer need.
  • Notices: if your role allows it, post a line that scrolls across the top of everyone's screen — on the web and on their phones — until you stop it. Tap it on the phone to stop it moving while you read.
  • Notifications on your phone for a new message, a group you are added to, and a notice sent as a push. Your phone registers itself when you sign in, and is forgotten when you sign out, so a shared phone never keeps your messages.
  • Unread counts, read receipts and "typing…" everywhere.
  • If your administrator has not yet connected the messaging service, everything still works — messages refresh every few seconds instead of instantly, and the Chats screen tells you which it is doing.
  • Already have the app installed? Ask your administrator to build it again, so the new Chats screen is in it.

November 2026 — v1.5.0 — your own mobile app

  • Your company now has its own Android app (iOS once your administrator sets up Apple signing) — same name, icon and colours as your platform, and it signs in to your company only.
  • Download it from Settings → Mobile App. On an Android phone, allow "Install unknown apps" for your browser the first time; later versions install over it.
  • Sign in with the same e-mail and password you use here. You see exactly what your role allows.
  • At the first sign-in the app shows your data-protection notice. It has to be read to the end before it can be accepted, and the acceptance appears under DPDP → Acceptance status marked as coming from the app.
  • The menu has Dashboard, Chats and Profile, where you sign out and can see the version and build number.

November 2026 — v1.4.0 — DPDP consent and your own website

DPDP consent (Settings → DPDP, and under Logs → DPDP)

  • Your consent notice: write it here, or upload your own PDF or Word file. You start from the platform's notice with your company's name, address and grievance officer already filled in — edit it and it becomes yours.
  • Share the consent link (your-address/consent) from your website, your apps and your CRM. The person must scroll the notice to the end before Accept turns on, and there is no way past it other than accepting or closing the window.
  • Every acceptance is kept as evidence: who, when, which version, how long they had it open, how far they scrolled, which purposes they ticked, and from where. Acceptance status lists them and downloads as Excel.
  • Cookie consent records what each visitor chose in the banner on your website.
  • Someone can ask you to withdraw their consent: use the ✕ on their row. The record stays and is marked withdrawn, as the Act requires.

Your own website (set up by your administrator)

  • A small site with a hero, your story, what you do, featured items, offers, testimonials, gallery, FAQ, contact details and an enquiry form — switch on only the sections you want.
  • Every enquiry on it becomes a lead, tagged with the campaign set on the Enquiry section, and the person's consent is recorded with it.

November 2026 — v1.3.0 — the company workspace (Super Admin)

  • A company now opens as its own page — click its name in Super Admin → Company. The header carries Force login, Login page, Suspend and Save changes; everything about the company sits behind its tabs.
  • Overview shows the company at a glance: leads, conversions, clients, outstanding, users, live channels, deliveries needing attention, its addresses and its latest leads.
  • Company details, Subscription (plan, frequency, amount, due date, discount in ₹ or %, gross) and Login credentials (with Show and Generate for the password).
  • Branding & domain adds login page colours and per-app themes; White label holds the platform-branding switch, support link, e-mail sender, app names, look & feel and custom CSS.
  • Role access lets Super Admin set the company's own roles, within the plan and the Modules tab.
  • Mobile Modules picks what the company's mobile apps may show.
  • Notifications sets each alert per device with its sound, including your own uploaded sounds.
  • Cron Jobs shows every background job with its schedule, last and next run, an on/off switch and Run now.
  • Retention Policy sets how long each log is kept, with a nightly housekeeping job and an Apply button.
  • Fixed: after a new deployment, clicking one menu then another could leave the screen where it was until a manual refresh. A click that does not land now takes you there directly.

November 2026 — v1.2.0 — deleting a client

  • Client → Clients has a Delete action next to View journey, verified by a one-time code on WhatsApp — the same gate used for leads.
    • Before any code is sent, you are shown exactly what goes with the client: sales order lines, unpaid invoices and their amount, pay-ins received and their amount, and tickets (with the open count). You can record a reason.
    • The code goes to your own WhatsApp number (your company's number if your profile has none) through the existing Delete OTP webhook event. It is valid for 5 minutes.
    • The client then leaves Clients, the Service Board, Subscription Management and its support page, together with its sales orders, invoices, pay-ins and tickets — so no stray rows are left behind.
  • Nothing is erased. A complete copy — profile, journey, sales orders, invoices, pay-ins and tickets — is archived in your company's own database, with who deleted it, when and why, and the same is written to the activity log. Payment files in S3 are left untouched. Ask your administrator if a deleted client has to be brought back.
  • Delete is a permission, and nobody gets it automatically. In Role Management, the Clients sub-module now has a Delete box. Unlike the other boxes it does not follow the Client module — a role can delete a client only once that box is ticked, so no existing role gained the ability on its own. The company owner is unaffected, and Super Admin can still restrict or pause it per company under Company → Modules.

November 2026 — v1.1.0

  • Sales Order shows one row per client, expanding to its services, with Convert to Invoice (Discount as a fixed amount or a percentage, and Gross).
  • Outstanding counts only what is due up to today; later months show as Upcoming.
  • Company Name on leads and clients, in the list, in search, in import and export, and in the sample file.
  • Integration → Needs attention lists any delivery that could not be saved as a lead, with Retry and Retry all.
  • WhatsApp Logs rebuilt, a more compact interface throughout, and release notes at /release.

October 2026 — sign-in connectors, Platform Apps, company modules

  • Facebook Lead Ads, Instagram Lead Ads, LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms and Google Sheets / Forms are now sign-in connectors:
    • Companies click Connect, give consent (DPDP Act), sign in on the platform and pick their Pages, accounts or sheet.
    • No App IDs, secrets or webhook setup for companies.
    • The old Facebook & Instagram App-ID setup is retired; existing connectors keep working.
  • Super Admin → Settings → Platform Apps:
    • Credovation’s Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps, with a Test button that also sets the Meta lead webhook.
    • An editable Privacy contact that appears on consent notices and on the new /privacy, /terms and /data-deletion pages.
  • Website / Landing Page Form and WhatsApp Business Platform are now REST API / webhook connectors, authenticated with the API key (older connectors keep working until switched).
  • Company → Modules tab: pause or restrict any module or sub-module per company, on top of the plan.
  • Knowledge Base tabs are written as Markdown files in the code (content/kb), so they update with every deploy.
    • Each article has Download .md and Copy Markdown, and Full guide (.md) gives every article in one file.
    • The Markdown is rebuilt on every deploy, with that deployment’s addresses filled in.

October 2026 — earlier

  • Role Management sub-modules.
  • Client billing renamed to Sales Order, Invoice and Pay-In.
  • A pop-up with S3 attachments when an invoice is marked Paid.
  • An “S3 storage required” switch per company.
